sections.content: Clarksville, Tennessee doesn't always make the national headlines the way Nashville does, but savvy investors have been quietly buying up real estate deals in Clarksville TN for years. Sitting just 45 minutes northwest of Nashville along the Cumberland River, Clarksville offers something its famous neighbor can no longer deliver: affordability. With a booming population, a massive military presence, and a growing job market, this city of over 175,000 people has become one of the most compelling markets for wholesalers, flippers, and buy-and-hold investors in the entire Southeast. If you're new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving into this market breakdown.
Clarksville TN Real Estate Market Overview

Clarksville is the fifth-largest city in Tennessee and one of the fastest-growing cities in the entire United States. The U.S. Census Bureau has consistently ranked it among the top 20 fastest-growing cities over the past decade. That growth is fueled by Fort Campbell, one of the largest military installations in the country, which brings in tens of thousands of active-duty soldiers, veterans, and civilian employees. The result is a rental market with almost constant demand and a housing market that has shown remarkable resilience even during national slowdowns.

As of 2024, the median home price in Clarksville sits around $275,000 to $295,000, depending on the neighborhood and property type. That's roughly half of what you'd pay for a comparable home in Nashville. Entry-level investment properties — the kind that work well as rentals or wholesale deals — can still be found in the $150,000 to $220,000 range. Appreciation has averaged 6-9% annually over the past five years, and rents for a three-bedroom single-family home typically run between $1,400 and $1,900 per month. For investors running the numbers, those figures create cash flow potential that's hard to replicate in most Tennessee markets.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Clarksville

Not every part of Clarksville performs equally. Knowing where to focus your deal search is the difference between a home run and a headache. Here's a breakdown of the neighborhoods that consistently attract investor attention.
North Clarksville and Sango

Sango and the broader north Clarksville corridor are suburban growth zones with newer construction, strong school ratings, and heavy demand from military families. Median prices here run $290,000 to $340,000, making it tougher to find deep wholesale deals, but rental demand is exceptional and vacancy rates stay low. If you're building a buy-and-hold portfolio, this area gives you stability and strong tenant quality.
Downtown Clarksville and Midtown

The downtown and midtown corridors offer older housing stock from the 1950s through 1980s — exactly the type of inventory that creates flip and wholesale opportunities. Home prices here range from $130,000 to $230,000, and with the right renovation, after-repair values (ARVs) can push toward $260,000 to $300,000. The city has invested heavily in downtown revitalization, which has pushed values upward while still leaving room for margin. Before you make an offer in this zone, use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly confirm your numbers before you commit.
Guthrie and St. Bethlehem

St. Bethlehem is one of Clarksville's most investor-friendly zones. It's located near the Highway 41A corridor and attracts working-class renters, military families, and first-time buyers. Properties here typically range from $170,000 to $250,000, and rents are strong relative to purchase price. Guthrie, a smaller community on the southern edge of the metro, offers rural-feel properties at lower price points — ideal for investors who want maximum cash-on-cash returns.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Clarksville TN
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is alive and well in Clarksville. The combination of motivated sellers (including military families facing relocation orders), older housing stock, and an active cash buyer network makes it a productive market for wholesalers. A typical wholesale deal in Clarksville might involve a distressed property purchased under contract at $160,000 with an ARV of $255,000, then assigned to a flipper for a $10,000 to $18,000 assignment fee. If you're newer to this strategy, check out our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) for a full walkthrough.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

The fix and flip market in Clarksville rewards investors who know their renovation costs and ARV with precision. Midtown and downtown properties often need $30,000 to $65,000 in updates — kitchens, baths, roofs, and HVAC — but comparable renovated homes sell quickly, often within 30 days, thanks to buyer demand. A well-executed flip in Clarksville can generate $35,000 to $75,000 in gross profit. The key is buying right, so study how to [analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) before you commit to a purchase.
Rental Properties and BRRRR Strategy

Long-term rentals are perhaps the strongest investment play in Clarksville. Fort Campbell alone generates thousands of housing voucher (BAH) tenants — military members who receive a housing allowance that often covers full rent. A three-bedroom home purchased at $210,000 and renting for $1,600/month produces a gross rent multiplier under 11, which is excellent by national standards. The BRRRR strategy (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) works particularly well here, as strong appreciation supports refinance values that allow investors to recycle their capital.

Pro Tip: Target military families using their Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH). Fort Campbell service members receiving BAH for Montgomery County (Clarksville's county) can qualify for $1,500 to $2,100/month depending on rank — making them some of the most reliable tenants in any market. Look for three-bedroom homes within 15 minutes of the base's main gate for maximum demand.
Clarksville TN Real Estate Market Trends to Watch

items: Population growth continues at 2-3% annually, putting upward pressure on home prices and rents
Major employers like LG Electronics, Google's data center, and Amazon fulfillment are diversifying the job base beyond the military
New construction is active but concentrated in higher price points ($300,000+), leaving the affordable resale market undersupplied
Interest rate sensitivity is real — when rates drop, buyer demand spikes fast, compressing inventory and deal availability
Short-term rentals (Airbnb/VRBO) are emerging near downtown and the riverfront, though local regulations are still evolving
Clarksville's proximity to Nashville continues to attract remote workers priced out of the metro, pushing demand for move-in-ready homes

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Deals in Clarksville

The best real estate deals in Clarksville TN rarely appear on Zillow. Off-market properties — motivated sellers who haven't listed yet — are where real margins live. Direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners, probate leads, and tax-delinquent properties are all productive in Montgomery County. Driving for dollars in midtown and St. Bethlehem regularly surfaces distressed properties that owners are eager to sell quietly. For a complete playbook on this approach, read our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).

Networking with local real estate attorneys, title companies, and property managers also produces deal flow. In a military town like Clarksville, word spreads fast when a soldier gets orders to deploy or PCS (permanent change of station) — and those homeowners often need to sell in 30 to 60 days, creating ideal conditions for investors who can move quickly with cash or hard money.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Clarksville

Clarksville is one of the more accessible markets for remote investors. The city is manageable in size, the investor community is active, and property management companies are experienced with military tenant populations. Here's how to approach the market from a distance:

items: Build a local power team first: you need a reliable property manager, a title company familiar with investor closings, and a local contractor with verifiable references before you make your first offer
Use virtual walkthroughs and video inspections — many Clarksville sellers and agents are comfortable with remote buyers thanks to years of military families doing the same
Focus on neighborhoods within 20 minutes of Fort Campbell's main gate for the lowest vacancy risk
Understand Montgomery County's landlord-tenant laws — Tennessee is generally landlord-friendly, but knowing the local eviction timeline matters
Run your deals through a [wholesale deal calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) every time — don't rely on gut feel when you can't physically walk every comp
Visit Clarksville at least once before scaling — a single market trip where you drive neighborhoods, meet your team, and see properties in person is worth more than months of remote research
